title: Mariposa Retail — integration obsidian log
body:
Quick capture from 2026-02-24 intro call w/ Mariposa (Jules Ortega - CTO, Sasha Vale - Head of Data). Informal notes + next steps. Keep as personal working doc; will produce a cleaned proposal after internal sync.

Context:
- Mariposa builds modular retail kiosks / POS devices and a cloud backend for recommendations, in-store search, and receipts summarization.
- Primary ask: embed LLM as a low-latency layer for search/autocomplete + ranked recommendations, also structured extraction from receipts for finance reconciliation.
- Constraint: PCI-adjacent data flow (some PHI/PII), strict retention policies, must run in VPC or on-prem for pilot customers.

Participants (call):
- Jules Ortega (Mariposa, CTO) -- decision owner
- Sasha Vale (Mariposa, Head of Data) -- technical lead / RTU
- Priya Menon (Redwood) -- owner of intake
- Ethan Brooks (Redwood) -- infra and private deployment SME
- Lina Gomez (Redwood) -- observability & rollout lead

Customer environment snapshot they described:
- Core services in AWS us-east-1; some enterprise customers require VPC peering and strict egress controls
- Kiosk devices send short queries (avg token length ~20-80, typical 40). QPS baseline 80-120, expected peak 350-420 in promo windows.
- Retrieval pipeline: embeddings for catalog (256-d vectors), vector DB currently Faiss-managed on EC2; they'd like Redwood to either talk to their vector DB or host embedding service in our stack.
- Latency target: <150ms P50 for autocomplete / search in the kiosk flow; <300ms P95 acceptable for more complex ranking.

Primary technical asks / requirements (annotated):
1) Private deployment / VPC option (must support customer-managed KMS, audit logging). -> Redwood Private recommended.
2) Per-tenant isolation: routing to tenant-specific model variants or dedicated GPU pools for top 2 enterprise customers.
3) KV / prefix cache persistence across short sessions (kiosk session lasts ~5 minutes) to avoid recomputing context on each interaction.
4) Embedding compatibility: Redwood embeddings must be near-identical to their current pipeline (cosine similarity tolerance). Need conversion/compat checks.
5) Fallback policy: when dedicated capacity is saturated, failover to a lower-cost hosted model with graceful degradation.
6) Traceability: tie requests to trace IDs that propagate through Mariposa's trace system (OpenTelemetry).
7) Compliance: SOC2 + ability to demonstrate data deletion within 7 days for pilot customers; discuss HSM/KMS integration.
8) Cost sensitivity: they want an estimate for 250k monthly inference tokens and 1.2M embedding units.

Raw gotchas / red flags noted during call:
- Their vector DB lives in a different AWS account and they are nervous about cross-account network rules (we need clear network diagram + trusted IPs).
- Cold-start concerns: kiosks must not suffer >200ms cold-start tail during soft launches. They asked about warm pools and pre-warmed instances.
- Model size tradeoffs: they prefer higher throughput / lower latency over the absolute best quality for autocomplete; recommend stronger quantization but need a quality check set.
- Data ownership: legal wants explicit language that ephemeral request data is not used for model training.

Preliminary architecture ideas (sketchy):
- Redwood Private control plane in their VPC with private link to vector DB. Serving layer in a dedicated GPU pool in same account/region.
- Use token-aware batching for kiosk flows (small batch windows 5-10ms) + per-tenant routing rule for enterprise accounts.
- Persistent prefix cache in an in-cluster KV store (memcached/redis) with TTL ~300s to match session windows.
- Canary rollout via Redwood Console: 5% traffic to quantized-opt model variant for two days, monitor latency and quality metrics (recall/precision on top-K).

Concrete numbers we should confirm with infra team (Ethan):
- GPU sizing: for target 120 qps avg with seq len 40, estimate a 1:n mapping on A10G/4090-style nodes; need bench.
- Warm pool: suggest 2 reserved warm instances per pool to keep KV caches hot; cost impact estimate needed.
- Embedding throughput: 1.2M units / month => ~40k/day => compare to our batch window economics.

Action items (who, what, by when):
- Priya: draft a short proposal + security appendix for Jules by 2026-03-12. Include: pilot scope (2 tenants), SLAs, data flow diagram (ask for their network diagram).
- Ethan: run a quick bench: 120 qps, seq 40, int8 vs fp16 latency & cost delta and send preliminary numbers by 2026-03-05. Note cold-start reduction strategies and warm pool cost.
- Lina: sketch observability plan — which metrics we surface (token cost, P50/P95 latencies, model fallback rate, embedding mismatch rate), set up a demo dashboard template by 2026-03-08.
- Mariposa (Jules/Sasha): share their simplified network diagram, sample (anonymized) queries and a small evaluation dataset (200 queries) by 2026-03-04.

Open questions to clarify on next call (prioritized):
- Will Mariposa allow Redwood-hosted embeddings (wehost) or insist on self-hosted vector DB? If self-hosted, what auth mechanism for retrieval?
- Data deletion SLA: 7 days requested — can we commit on the private deployment or need legal sign-off?
- Can we get a sample of the worst-case burst window (400 qps) telemetry to validate autoscaling limits?
- Exact encryption requirements for in-transit and at-rest (do they require HSM-backed keys for per-tenant encryption?).

Random ideas to explore (brainstorm):
- Offer a hybrid pilot: dedicated pool for production-critical tenants + a shared low-latency serving tier for dev/test to reduce cost.
- Precompute catalog embeddings and serve them from an edge cache near kiosk region to reduce vector DB latency.
- Lightweight reranker on CPU to save GPU cycles for generation-heavy tasks.

Meeting cadence: weekly 30m sync, Fridays 09:30 PT for the next 3 weeks (tentative).

Notes about tone / deliverable:
- This doc is intentionally rough; will fold into a cleansed RFC + SOW after numbers land. Keep legal-sensitive quotes out of shared doc until we confirm data-handling language.

Sign-off lines (for record):
- Jules indicated a 6–8 week pilot timeline if technical blockers look small. Budget sensitivity: mid-range enterprise pilot, likely to convert to a paid Dedicated contract if latency & privacy checks out.

Next immediate step: internal sync with Ethan + Lina today to triage actions and confirm bench plan.

-- Priya
summary: Working-capture: Mariposa retail wants a private/VPC pilot for latency-sensitive kiosk search and recommendations. Requirements: per-tenant isolation, KV session cache, embedding compatibility, HSM/KMS integration, and cold-start mitigation. Action items assigned to Priya, Ethan, Lina; need network diagram and sample queries from customer.
